simple.meaning: אֹשׁ (ʼôsh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a foundation.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 4:12. The surrounding context includes sacrifice, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֹשׁ (H787) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אֹשׁ (ʼôsh) / H787 is traced through Ezra 4:12, Ezra 5:16, Ezra 6:3 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H787. osh [ אשׁ K § 55, 5 c ] noun masculine Ezra 6:3 foundation (probably loan-word from Assyrian uššû , id. , √ אשׁשׁ (see Biblical Hebrew), so Zim KAT 3. 649 ; ᵑ7 feminine אוּשָׁא , Late Hebrew אוּשָׁה , Christian- Palestinian Aramaic , , Schulth Lex. 19 ; Arabic : Nö M 99 ); — plural emphatic אֻשַּׁיָּא 4:12 ; 5:16 ; suffix אֻשֹּׁהִי 6:3 .

occurrences.englishText: Be it known to the king that the Jews who came up from you have come to us to Jerusalem. They are building the rebellious and bad city, and have finished the walls, and repaired the foundations.
Then the same Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of God’s house which is in Jerusalem. Since that time even until now it has been being built, and yet it is not completed.

In the first year of Cyrus the king, Cyrus the king made a decree: Concerning God’s house at Jerusalem, let the house be built, the place where they offer sacrifices, and let its foundations be strongly laid; with its height sixty cubits,* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. and its width sixty cubits;
